claims.nodeLabel: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Pub. L. 83-703, 68 Stat. 919)
claims.text: The Statutes at Large header reads 'Public Law 703 / CHAPTER 1073 / August 30, 1954 / [H. R. 9757]', at 68 Stat. 919. Its long title is 'To amend the Atomic Energy Act of 1946, as amended, and for other purposes', so the 1954 Act is a complete restatement of the 1946 Act rather than a repeal of it.

claims.nodeLabel: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Pub. L. 83-703, 68 Stat. 919)
claims.sourceText: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 secs. 11 r. and 141-145 against Atomic Energy Act of 1946 sec. 10, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-68/pdf/STATUTE-68-Pg919.pdf and https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-60/pdf/STATUTE-60-Pg755.pdf
claims.text: WHAT CHANGED FROM 1946, FROM THE TWO TEXTS SIDE BY SIDE. The 1946 Act defined 'restricted data' only 'as used in this section', at section 10; the 1954 Act makes 'Restricted Data' a capitalised, Act-wide definition in the definitions chapter. 1954 ADDS the word 'design'. 'Fissionable material' and 'production of power' become 'special nuclear material' and 'production of energy'. And the 1946 carve-out was open-ended Commission discretion, where 1954 ties removal to a formal declassification procedure at section 142, including the transclassification of weapons-utilisation data into 'defense information' under section 142 d.

claims.sourceText: Atomic Energy Act of 1954, term search over the enacted text, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-68/pdf/STATUTE-68-Pg919.pdf
claims.text: THE PHRASE 'BORN CLASSIFIED' APPEARS NOWHERE IN THE ACT. A text search returns zero occurrences, and there is no express automatic-classification clause. The doctrine is an inference from the breadth of the section 11 r. definition taken together with the criminal provisions at sections 224 to 227, and it should be written as the inference it is rather than as statutory language.

claims.sourceText: Atomic Energy Act of 1946, sec. 2(a)(4)(B), https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-60/pdf/STATUTE-60-Pg755.pdf ; Atomic Energy Act of 1954, Public Law 83-703, 68 Stat. 919, sec. 25, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-68/pdf/STATUTE-68-Pg919.pdf
claims.text: A Division of Military Application under a serving officer was in the Commission from the start: the 1946 Act establishes it alongside Research, Production and Engineering and provides that 'The Director of the Division of Military Application shall be a member of the armed forces.' The 1954 Act carries it forward at section 25 with the Director required to be 'an active member of the Armed Forces.'

b.label: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Pub. L. 83-703, 68 Stat. 919)

edges.label: Excludes Restricted Data from the executive classification system
edges.note: Section 13 leaves Atomic Energy Act Restricted Data outside the order's reach. This is the seam between the two regimes: one body of information in United States law is classified by statute and not by executive order, and the executive order says so itself. Note the order predates the 1954 Act by ten months and the exclusion runs to the Atomic Energy Act as it then stood.
